title: Building a Place to Make Things

paragraphs.en: The abandoned cottage behind the student dormitory looked like a mess, but Lin saw the possibility of a shared workshop. A leaking pipe crossed the courtyard, a barrel blocked the entrance, and a stack of damaged chairs reached almost to the ceiling. The former owner had used a nearby hut as a store for gardening equipment. Turning this neglected space into a place for making things would require more than enthusiasm. Lin began with a diary of necessary repairs and invited neighbors to contribute skills rather than merely donate money.
paragraphs.zh: 学生宿舍后废弃的小屋看起来乱糟糟的，但林看到了把它改为共享工坊的可能。漏水管穿过院子，木桶挡着入口，一摞损坏椅子几乎堆到天花板。以前的主人用旁边小棚存园艺工具。把被忽视的空间变成制作东西的地方，需要的不只是热情。林开始用日记记录必要维修，并邀请邻居贡献技能，而不只是捐钱。

paragraphs.en: The first volunteers cleared the garage and repaired the bathroom. A wooden stake marked the path, keeping visitors away from the trash awaiting collection. They filled a bucket from a safe water tank and removed garbage before touching any electrical fittings. An experienced builder examined every stair and replaced a loose nail near the landing. A lamp restored light to the working area, and a cord was secured so nobody would trip. A closet became storage for each repair kit, while a shelf held a jar of spare screws. A parcel from a local warehouse supplied gloves and protective glasses, turning safety from an abstract warning into an ordinary routine.
paragraphs.zh: 第一批志愿者清理车库并修好浴室。木桩标明小路，让访客远离等待清运的垃圾。他们从安全水箱取水装桶，在接触电气装置前先清除垃圾。经验丰富的建筑工检查每级台阶，更换平台附近松动的钉子。灯让工作区重新明亮，电线也固定好，以免绊倒人。壁橱用于存放维修工具包，架子上放着装备用螺丝的罐子。本地仓库寄来手套和护目镜，使安全从抽象警告变成日常程序。

paragraphs.en: The layout divided noisy work from quieter activities. In one corner, a pottery teacher demonstrated how a lump of clay became a pot, explaining how an oven differed from the kiln needed for firing. A metal rod supported the display shelf. Nearby, a volunteer repaired fabric with a needle and thread, teaching learners to recognize texture before choosing a stitch. A bunch of damaged cushions supplied practice material. A stove and a pan served simple meals, but cooking remained separate from dust and chemicals. Participants learned that careful organization could protect creativity rather than restrict it.
paragraphs.zh: 空间布局把嘈杂作业与安静活动分开。一角，陶艺老师展示一团黏土如何变成陶罐，说明普通烤箱与烧制陶器所需窑炉的差别。金属杆支撑着展示架。附近，志愿者用针线修补织物，教学习者在选择针法前辨别质地。一批破损靠垫提供练习材料。炉灶和平底锅用于做简单饭菜，但烹饪区与粉尘、化学品分开。大家认识到，认真组织空间可以保护创造力，而非限制它。

paragraphs.en: As the workshop grew, its members noticed needs they had not anticipated. Someone living in a small cabin requested a portable shelf; another brought a broken cage that could be safely converted into a plant holder. A discarded tent became waterproof packaging, and a tablet helped participants photograph each stage of a repair. Ink labels identified the owner of every object, including a decorative ornament and a bicycle accessory. In the small lounge, older visitors explained earlier repair traditions while waiting for assistance. People who disliked formal classes often learned most readily through these unplanned conversations.
paragraphs.zh: 工坊发展后，成员发现了原本没有预想到的需求。住在小木屋的人想要便携架子，另一个人带来破笼子，可以安全改成花架。废弃帐篷变成防水包装，平板电脑帮助大家拍摄维修步骤。墨水标签注明每件物品的主人，包括装饰品和自行车配件。在小休息区，老年访客等候帮助时讲述从前的修理传统。不喜欢正式课程的人，常常在这些自然发生的交流中学得最好。

paragraphs.en: At an evening gathering, a candle illuminated photographs of the cottage before renovation. A child placed a flower basket beside them, and someone joked that the place deserved a warm bath after all its years of neglect. The group did not pretend to have eliminated waste or poverty. They had created a reliable place to ask for help, experiment, and return when an attempt failed. Their success depended less on any impressive machine than on the willingness to share tools, explain mistakes, and make room for learners who had arrived with uncertainty.
paragraphs.zh: 一次晚间聚会中，蜡烛照亮了小屋翻修前的照片。孩子在照片旁放了花篮，有人笑说，这地方被忽视多年，如今值得好好洗个热水澡。团体没有假装已经消除浪费或贫困，而是建成一个可靠的场所，让人求助、尝试，并在失败后再来。他们的成功与其说依赖先进机器，不如说依赖分享工具、解释错误，以及给满怀不确定的新学员留出空间的意愿。
